title: Clone Pattern with Linked Editing – Symmetry Pattern (with Sewing)
content: **List of Contents** Symmetry Pattern (With Sewing) Apply Symmetry Pattern (With Sewing) **Symmetry Pattern (With Sewing)** \- Duplicate Patterns symmetrically with the linked editing function to edit Patterns and Sewing Lines at the same time. **Apply Symmetry Pattern (With Sewing)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=exDXe-fAeFk \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021849587/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021911008/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool \- Right-click on the Pattern to be duplicated and select Clone Pattern with Linked Editing – **Symmetry Pattern (With Sewing).** \- The duplicated Pattern will follow along with the mouse cursor. \- Click on the 2D window to paste the duplicated Pattern. \- The symmetrized Patterns will be highlighted in blue. \- Since the Patterns are symmetrized, they can be edited symmetrically at the same time along with their Sewing Lines. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore the features of the Symmetry Pattern tool that allows you to duplicate and edit sewing patterns symmetrically for efficient design creation.

title: Clone as Reference Line
content: **Clone as Reference Line** * **Clone as Reference Line ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6eb2kFjTbBY \- Create a Reference Line to refer to when editing a Pattern \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Right-click on the Pattern and select **Clone as Reference Line** from the pop-up menu. \- A Reference Line will be created. \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. Then, click and drag to move the desired point or line on the Pattern. \- The original shape of the Pattern will appear as a Reference Line.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to create and utilize a Reference Line in pattern editing using the "Clone as Reference Line" feature in Clo3D.

title: Clone as Internal Shape
content: **Clone as Internal Shape** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UuM9tnmBNT4 \- Create an Internal Shape identical to a Pattern. \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021849587/mceclip0.png) **Transform pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021911008/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right click on the desired pattern and select **Clone as Internal Shape.** \- The duplicated Internal Shape will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Click on the 2D window to paste the duplicated Internal Shape. \- The selected Pattern will be cloned as an Internal Shape.
content_description: Learn how to effortlessly create an Internal Shape that mirrors a pattern in Clo3D by following our step-by-step guide and video tutorial.

title: Colorway Multiview Snapshot
content: **List of Contents** Colorway Multiview Snapshot Capturing Colorway Multiview Snapshot **Colorway Multiview SnapshotYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BhF_0M9n7BE ** \- Capture multiview snapshot of a single garment or an outfit in multiple colorways at one time. \- Switch to Colorway Mode. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ FILE ▶ Snapshot ▶ **3D Window** to create and save a Snapshot. **Capturing Colorway Multiview SnapshotYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bksr8YiUpgo ** \- Switch to Colorway Mode and navigate to File ▶ Snapshot ▶**3D Window**. \- A file browser will appear. \- Assign file name and its saving location. Then, select Save. \- Snapshot pop-up window will appear. \- Check **Save All Colorways** under Options category. Select Save. \- Multiview snapshot of the 3D Garment in multiple colorways will be saved at the designated location. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for capturing and saving multiview snapshots of garments in various colorways using the Colorway Mode feature.

title: 3D Garment View Controls
content: **List of Contents** Change Camera View Zoom In/Out Shortcuts Zoom to Selected Zoom in and change view in the 3D window at once. **Change Camera View** Right click on the 3D window to access the pop-up menu. Select the desired view among Front, 3/4 Left, Back, Left, Right, 3/4 Right, Top, Button, or use respective shortcuts (2, 3, 8, 6, 4, 1, 5, 0) to change camera view instantly. **Camera Direction Change Standards** Using the corresponding menu while the avatar is facing a different direction on the screen changes the camera's angle according to the avatar. **Zoom In/Out Shortcuts** **Zoom In:** Hold down the + key on the keyboard to zoom in the 3D window. **Zoom Out:** Hold down the - key on the keyboard to zoom out the 3D window. **Zoom to Selected** Zoom in/out and rotate the 3D window using the selected Pattern or item as the focal point. Select the desired Pattern or item in the 3D window and locate Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ **Zoom Extends All** , Or press the shortcut key F to enlarge the selected object at a fixed scale at the middle and control the view according to it. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides essential shortcuts and instructions for efficiently changing camera views and zooming in and out in a 3D environment.

title: Show/Hide Seam Allowance
content: ### **Objective** Show or hide seam allowances from the 2D window. Seam allowances can be shown and hidden in the Print Layout Mode as well. ** Location ** **For versions 5.0 and later:** Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Show Seam Allowance** 2D Window ▶ 2D Pattern Display ▶ **Show Seam Allowance** **For versions 4.2 and earlier:** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern**** **2D Toolbar ▶![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36783351426329) **Transform Pattern** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated location above based on your software version: 2. For **versions 5.0 and later** , follow the path to the option either through the main menu or the vertical toggle bar in the 2D window. The seam allowances can be hidden again using the same path. 3. For **versions 4.2 and earlier** , right-click into the empty space of the 2D window: → In the right-click menu, select**Show Seam Allowance**. Repeat this to hide seam allowances again. **※Note:** All seam allowances remain shown when the ![seam_allowance.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36783335099545) **Seam Allowance** tool is activated.
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for displaying and hiding seam allowances in the 2D window and Print Layout Mode for different software versions.

title: [CLO-SET] Upload to CLO-SET
content: ### **Objective** Upload 3D files and share them easily with others. ** Location ** Main Menu ▶ CLO-SET ▶ Upload to CLO-SET ▶ **Project/Garment/Avatar** ** Operation** 1. Create a project. 2. Follow the location outlined above. → You will be directed to the upload page on CLO-SET. → For **Network OnlineAuth** users: If you are not a registered member of CLO-SET, you are directed to the sign up page. **※ Note:** For detailed instruction on how to use CLO-SET, please refer to the **[CLO-SET Help Center](https://support.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/categories/4405849186447-GETTING-STARTED)**.
content_description: Easily upload and share your 3D files by creating a project on CLO-SET.

title: Assign to New Fabric
content: **Assign to New Fabric** * **Assign to New Fabric ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qs1dhh0kRbA \- Add a new fabric item and apply it to the selected Patterns simultaneously. \- Select Patterns using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021908028/mceclip0.png) Transform Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the Patterns to access the pop-up menu. Select **Assign to New Fabric.** A new fabric item will be added and applied to the selected Patterns.
content_description: Learn how to efficiently add and apply a new fabric item to selected patterns using the Transform Pattern tool in this step-by-step guide.

title: Optimize All Curve Points
content: **Optimize All Curve Points** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gVIXoamGcT0 \- Easily edit curves by optimizing the number of curve points on segments. Use this function when there are unnecessarily many curve points. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022574027/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar to see all curve points on Patterns. \- Right-click on the 2D window and select **Optimize All Curve Points** from the pop-up menu. Surplus curve points will be deleted and only the necessary curve points needed to maintain the shape of the curves will be remained.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to optimize curve points in your designs, ensuring cleaner patterns by removing unnecessary curve points for improved editing efficiency.

title: V-Ray Render Image/Video Properties
content: **List of Contents** Image/Video Properties Image/Video Image Size Color Correction Background Save Open/Save Image/Video Properties **Image/Video Properties ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p-LE9SBjElM \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026473148/mceclip0.png) **Image/Video Properties** tool from the Render toolbar and navigate to the Property Editor. ** Image/Video YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lYoGlUfpf28 ** \- Select the medium for the final Render product among Image, Turntable Images, and Turntable Video. * **Image** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=toGlTvPnjtk \- Extract rendered 3D Garment as an image. * **View Point** * **Current View** \- Render the 3D Garment as it is shown in the 3D window. * **Custom View** \- Render the 3D Garment with a Custom View. * **Render All Colorways** All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). * **Turntable Images ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nuHoLLLoFGY \- Extract rendered 3D Garment as multiple images, showing it in 360°. * **Image Count** \- Decide the number of images to be rendered. \- Higher the Image Count is, from more viewpoints the 3D Garment is rendered. * **Direction** * **Counterclockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered counterclockwise. * **Clockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered clockwise. * **Render All Colorways** All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). * **Turntable Video** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I06tDemxstA\- Extract rendered 3D Garment as a video rotating in 360° * **Video Frame Count** \- Decide the number of images to be rendered and stitched as a video. \- Higher the Video Frame Count, more smoothly the video rotates. * **Duration** \- Decide the total duration of the video. \- Expand the child menu to find Video Frame Duration, which decides the duration per frame. * **Direction** * **Counterclockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered counterclockwise. * **Clockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered clockwise. * **Video Codec** \- Select the video codec used for recording. * **Render All Colorways** All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). **Image Size YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rf8HfrfQoxE ** \- Set the dimension of rendered images or videos. \- Choose among provided presets or select Custom to freely configure the width and height of the images or videos as needed. * **Orientation** * **Portrait** \- The image is laid out vertically. * **Landscape** \- The image is laid out horizontally. * **Width** \- Set image’s width * **Height** \- Set image’s height * **Maintain Ratio** \- Lock Width and Height ratio by toggling on the Maintain Ratio option. **Color Correction YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mD3iDfUr-bM ** * **Exposure** \- Set how much the image is exposed to light. \- Higher the Exposure value is, brighter the image is. * **Contrast** \- Set how strong the bright and dark areas are contrasted. \- Higher the Contrast value is, stronger the contrast gets. **Background YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_xOG0L70SZ0 ** * **Color** \- Set the color of the background. * **Transparency** \- Set the background image as transparent. **Save YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D5SSR8rUcKs ** * **File Name** \- Decide the name of the saved images. * **File Path** \- Locate the saving path for the images. **Open/Save Image/Video Properties YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6Jv-fWt1ifY ** * **Open** \- Open previously saved Image/Video Properties. * **Save** \- Save configured Image/Video Properties and apply to other files. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for configuring and managing image and video properties in 3D garment rendering, featuring detailed instructions and helpful video resources.

title: [Style Property] Button
content: Change color and texture of buttons as desired. #### 1. Click the Button style in Button tab in Object Browser. **** 2. Adjust the properties referring to the following as needed. **Options** | **Desciption**** ** ---|--- **Information** | **Name/ Item NO.** ** **| Enter a name and an item number of the button. **Tech Pack** **(CLO-SET)**** ** | Set whether you include the button in the Tech Pack or not. **Shape**** **| **Thread Type** | Set the type of thread (Cross, Parallel, Square) **Width**** **| Set the width of the button. User Settings ▶ [User setting](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001547128) you can change the button unit to L. **Link to Fastend Buttonhole****(ver 2024.1)** | If the button is fastened, you can automatically apply the width change to the fastened buttonhole as well. **Thickness** | Set the thickness of the button. **Weigh** | Set the weigh of the button. **Material** | Set the [Material](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/360047317454-%EC%9B%90%EB%8B%A8-%EC%9E%AC%EC%A7%88-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95) of the button. If you turn off **Use Same Material as Button** option in the Thread tab, you can set those materials separately. #### ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39592740944921) ## **![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39592727165337) **You can apply metal easily with the newly provided metal presets. ![25. Button Metal Preset.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39592727165721)
content_description: Customize the color and texture of buttons with detailed settings for shape, material, and dimensions to enhance your design.

title: V-Ray Render Light Properties
content: **List of Contents** Light Properties Environment Map Light Intensity Rectangle Light Open/Save Settings **Light Properties YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bFCvu1DpMDw **\- Set lighting properties applied to final render output. \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026363368/mceclip0.png) **Light Properties** tool from the render toolbar and navigate to the Property Editor. ** Environment Map YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k0o1HqcBmdg **\- The **environment map** is a lighting setting processed into an image format. \- By default, six different environment maps are provided. \- Select the desired environment map as needed. **Light Intensity YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vFTv9Ozi1-U ** \- Adjust the brightness of the 3D Garment in the final rendered image by configuring the Light Intensity. \- The default value is 1.00 and the setting can be adjusted between 0.00 and 4.00. \- Higher the value is, brighter the 3D Garment is. **Rectangle Light YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GFP4F8prd_k ** \- Add and modify point lights up to three. \- Adjust lights' location with the Gizmo tool. * **Intensity ** \- Adjust the intensity of the light. * **Color ** \- Set the color of the light. * **Width ** \- Set the width of the light. * **Height ** \- Set the height of the light. * **Show ** \- Show or hide the light from the 3D window. **※ Note :** * To create a three-dimensional render image, there must be a key light. Add key lights as needed to create more dynamic images. * When the Rectangle Lights are used along with the Dome Light, use a HDRI image without a key light. **Open/Save Settings YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F2C5rWBwKoI ** * **Open ** \- Click the Open button on the right top corner of the Property Editor to load previously saved Light Properties. * **Save ** \- Click the Save button on the right top corner of the Property Editor to save the configuration. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for configuring lighting properties in 3D rendering, including environment maps, light intensity adjustments, rectangle light settings, and options for saving and loading configurations.

title: PBR Map Generator (ver 2024.1)
content: ### **Objective** Generate PBR maps (Normal, Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, Metalness Maps) for realistic texture expresssion from a basic texture image. **Location ** Texture Property Editor ▶ Each PBR Map Properties ▶ ![PBR.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33852438547481)**PBR Map Generator** ** Operation** 1. Load a texture image from the object properties whose [fabric](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047317454-Set-Fabric-Textures) and material you want to change. 2. Select the tool/menu in Location. → Each PBR map is automatically generated based on the texture image.
content_description: Create realistic PBR maps from basic texture images to enhance your 3D models' visual quality using the PBR Map Generator in the Texture Property Editor.

title: Create Ellipse
content: **List of Contents** Ellipse Create Ellipse **Ellipse** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OGdaXC2ZLtQ \- Create Ellipse or circle in 2D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar. ** Create Ellipse** * **Free-hand an Ellipse YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sxHmjZR1yPw ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. \- Click and drag on the 2D window as the preview of an Ellipse appears. \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a Circle. \- When the desired shape of an Ellipse or a Circle is achieved, release the mouse. \- An Ellipse or a Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. * **Use Diameter & Radius YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6nXIZcSuToE **\- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. ** -** Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse Window appears. \- Enter desired values for**Width** ,**Height** , **Diameter** , and**Radius**. Then, hit OK. \- An Ellipse or a Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. * **Use Circumference YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BIpY8PJQ0Zk ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. \- Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse window appears. \- Enter desired values for **Circumference.** \- An Ellipse or Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. ** ** * **Create and Replicate Ellipses YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7zeIj_wksVg ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. \- Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse window appears. \- **Interval** : type in the distance between the Ellipses. \- **Angle** : type in the angle that replicated Ellipses will be created. \- **Number of Shapes** : type in the number of Ellipses to be replicated. \- Click OK. \- The Ellipses are created based on the settings above. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide and tutorial videos on how to create and manipulate ellipses and circles in a 2D design window using the Ellipse tool.

title: Add Point/Split Line
content: **List of Contents** Add Point/Split Line Add Point Split into Two Lines Split by Length Uniform Split **Add Point/ Split Line** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aMFIJW6sv-E \- Add point to Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to split them. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Add Point/Split Line.** ** Add Point** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=91_mK0K3IAs \- Add point to Pattern outlines. \- Add point to Internal Lines. **Split into Two Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4pM4RxsazPo \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/ Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. Then, right click on a segment and select **Split. ** \- The Split Line window will appear. Click **Split into Two Lines. ** \- The selected line will be divided into two different length segments on the basis of the purple guide point. The desired length can be entered in the Line 1, the shorter segment and the Line 2, the longer segment. \- The selected line will be divided into two different length segments on the basis of the purple guide point. The proportion of each segment can be entered in the Line 1, the shorter segment and the Line 2, the longer segment. **Split by Length** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_iPcukEJ8Qg \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/ Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. Then, right click on a segment and select **Split. ** \- The Split Line window will appear. Click **Split by Length. ** \- **Segment Length** : points will be added to the line with the Segment Length Interval, starting from one side of the line. \- **Number of Segments** : set how many segments the line will be divided into. \- **Direction** : set toward which direction the points will be added. **Uniform Split** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Cm0Jkt2zWc \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. Then, right click on a segment and select **Split. ** \- The Split Line window will appear. Click **Uniform Split. ** \- **Number of Segments** : set how many segments the line will be equally divided into. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on utilizing the "Add Point/Split Line" tool in 2D pattern design, featuring instructional videos and step-by-step instructions for various splitting techniques.

title: Edit Piping
content: **List of Contents** Edit Piping Select Piping Edit Length Edit Piping Properties Piping Right Click Pop-Up Menu **Edit Piping** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HRlB8hFZNTs \- Select and edit Pipings on 3D Garments. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Piping ▶ **Edit Piping** ** ****Select Piping** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7nwPB8rv1Wc \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool selected, click on the Piping on the 3D Garment. \- The selected Piping will be highlighted in yellow. **Edit Length** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JKQ29x65b0U \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool selected, click and drag either end of the Piping towards the direction it will be abridged or extended. **Edit Piping Properties** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yCOxCmFtHQ0 \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool or the **Select/Move** , click the Piping on the 3D Garment and navigate the Property Editor. \- The selected Piping’s properties will appear. * **Name** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NF2_-Uczhwg \- View and edit the name of the selected Piping. * **Line Length** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z49uvAdpb60 \- View the length of the selected Piping. * **Width** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kZ-t0unGSfE \- View the length of the selected Piping. * **Particle Distance** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qsXXaznbDaQ \- View and edit the Particle Distance of the selected Piping. \- The Piping’s Particle Distance is set as 1.5mm by default. \- Narrower the Piping’s width is, smaller the Particle Distance should be. * **Hide** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qhYY4v5MaHw \- Toggle on or off the **Hide** checkbox to hide or show the selected Piping. \- The Piping will appear translucent when the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool is activated, but it will disappear when other 3D tools are activated. * **Fabric** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hes_dZzaufc \- Change the fabric material for the selected Piping. \- The options appear in the list are the fabric lists in the Object Browser. **Piping Right Click Pop-Up Menu** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oJmpqTsJCOw \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022184048/mceclip1.png) **Select/Move** tool, right click on the Piping to access the right-click pop-up menu. * **Delete** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_qL1xBAVkr4 \- Delete the selected Piping. \- Select the Piping and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. * **Refresh All Piping** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QS4srMHE6EQ \- Re-drape all Pipings on the 3D Garment. \- Use this to re-simulate Pipings that distorted while simulating the 3D Garment. * **Deactivate** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UX9lrc6-waQ \- Deactivate the selected Piping. \- Right-click again on the deactivated piping. The **Deactivate** option should have changed to the **Activate** option. Select **Activate** to activate the piping. * **Freeze** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uqJ1NiY3NTA \- Freeze the piping to exclude it from the simulation. \- Right-click again on the frozen piping. The **Freeze** option should have changed to the **Unfreeze** option. Select **Unfreeze** to unfreeze the piping. * **Quadrangulate** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TkTBDcpVF_c \- Change the Piping’s mesh structure to rectangles. * **Triangulate** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iAT4B3MJFsg \- Change the Piping’s mesh structure to triangles. * **Hide** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tto1EqGrq2k \- Hide the selected Piping. \- The Piping wiil appear translucent when the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool is activated, but it will disappear when other 3D tools are activated. \- To show the hidden Piping, select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool and right click on the Piping. The **Hide** option should have changed to the **Show** option. \- Select the **Show** option to show the selected Piping. * **Show All PipingYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nRIvtUxtH1E -** Show all hidden Pipings. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for selecting and editing piping on 3D garments, featuring step-by-step instructions and instructional videos for various piping modifications.

title: Fasten Button
content: **List of Contents** Fasten Button Fastening Buttons and Buttonholes Unfastening Buttons and Buttonholes **Fasten Button YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bSFvN7XjNC8 ** \- title: Buttonhole
content: **List of Contents** Buttonhole Creating a Buttonhole **ButtonholeYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LwfuXnvpF1A** \- Create Buttonholes on 3D garment. \- Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001028728/Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png)**Buttonhole** tool from the 3D toolbar. **Creating a Buttonhole** * **Create a Buttonhole ManuallyYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=65xzqy6k8X8 ** \- Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001028728/Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png)**Buttonhole** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Navigate to either the 3D Window or the 2D Window and hover the mouse over where the Buttonhole will be created as a red dot appears to guide the location. \- Click on the desired location to create a Buttonhole. * **Create a Buttonhole with Designated ValuesYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJNmOwPkB2I ** \- Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001028728/Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png)**Buttonhole** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D Window and hover the mouse over where the Buttonhole will be created as smart guidelines appear. \- Right-click on the desired location to access a pop-up window. title: Buttonhole Properties
content: **Adjust buttonhole properties such as Transformation and 2D Measurements. ** #### 1. Click on the Buttonhole using the ![Edit Button On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38020483609497) **Select/Move Button** tool in the 3D toolbar. 2. Adjust the Buttonhole properties. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Style** | Select a buttonhole style. **Buttonhole** **Transformation****** | **Angle** | Enter the desired value for Rotation Angle of buttonholes. **Z-Offset** | ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38044041419033) Even when the buttonhole is hidden due to additional thickness and displacement maps on fabrics, adjusting the Z-Offset can make it visible. **Bind Position** | Change the bind position of the buttonhole by percentage (%). It can also be entered in units of the program setting. **2D Measurement** | Check the position of the buttonhole in the 2D pattern (left/right/top/bottom) with Measurement.

content: **List of Contents** Basic Circumference Measurement Measure Circumference **Basic Circumference Measurement** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BDItfpcPWBQ \- Measure a circumference of an Avatar. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021847927/mceclip0.png) **Basic Circumference Measurement** tool from the 3D toolbar or navigate to Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ **Basic Circumference Measurement.** ** Measure Circumference** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RZvb8LbvJBM \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021847947/mceclip1.png) **Basic Circumference Measurement** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Left click the total of three times to measure the Avatar’s circumference. \- Click once to start the Circumference Measurement, then move the mouse and click again to assign the measurement direction. \- Hover the mouse over the purple line connecting the first and the second point and move the mouse to assign the circumference angle. \- When the desired circumference angle is achieved, left click to complete the Circumference Measurement. \- After establishing the first point of the circumference, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create the second and third point in a straight line. title: Grainline
content: ## **New in 2024.2** **** **List of Content** **Grain Direction** **Link All Colorways** **Grain Orientation** **Grainline Lock** #### **Adjust the direction and orientation of the grainline, while also being able to lock Grainline properties and adjustments across all modes and features within CLO. ** 1. Click the 2D pattern using the ![Transform Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37931791249049)**Transform Pattern** or ![Edit Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37931791261337)**Edit Pattern** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. Adjust the direction and orientation of the grainline in the Property Editor. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37932578723609) ** ** **Grain Direction** | The main angle/ degree for the pattern's placement on the fabric roll. 1) Click the text field. 2) Press the arrow keys on the keyboard to change the degree based on how the Grain Orientation is set up. Examples: • Grain Orientation One way: The numbers will switch every 45 degrees. • Grain Orientation Two Or Four Way: The numbers will switch every 90 Degrees. 3) Or enter a specific degree. ---|--- **Link All Colorways** | If there are multiple colorways within the project file checking this checkbox on will apply the grainline information to all colorways. If the checkbox is unchecked that means each colorway can be different. ****📝****Note:****_This could be helpful if you want more control when entering production or if you are planning on having different fabrics for different colorways._ **Grain ****Orientation** | To decide how many different orientations/ directions the pattern can be placed on the fabric roll. **📝 Note:**_These options are very important for when moving into production and learning how much it would cost to produce the garment. This is also very important because based on the fabric you have applied certain the different orientations will change how much or how little stretch the garment has._ ** One Way ** | The pattern should only be placed in that one orientation that is dictated by the Grain Direction degree. ** Two Way ** | The pattern can be placed in two different orientation. The degree dictated by the Grain Direction and the degree that is the direct opposite (_180 degree from the original_). Examples: • 0 Degree Original: 180 Degree second option. • 90 Degree Original: 270 Degree Second option. ** Four Way ** | The pattern can be placed in four different orientations. The degree dictated by the Grain Direction and any other orientation that 90 degree from the original degree. Examples: • 0 Degree Original: 90,180,270 other options. • 45 Degree Original: 135,225,315 other options. **Grainline Lock** | Checking this on will lock the grainline across all modes of CLO. Stopping any adjustments to the grainline when working with other tools or functions within CLO that can adjust the Grainline. ****📝****Note:****_This locking is very helpful to keep continuity across all of CLO._ _The Print Layout mode and the Edit Texture tools will be the parts of CLO that are affected the most when checking this on or off._ * *
content_description: Explore the new features in CLO 2024.2 that enhance your control over grain direction and orientation, allowing for precise adjustments and consistent properties across all colorways and modes.

title: Seam Taping
content: **Reinforce edges of Patterns to withstand from drooping down by gravity when Simulating.** 1. Click on the ![Seam Taping On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37880812122905) **Seam Taping** tool on the 2D toolbar. 2. Select a segment Pattern to reinforce, or Click-and-drag also allows applying seam tapes. 3. Activate the ![Simulation Normal On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37881774490393) **Simulate**. → The seam tape is now being applied to the selected segment and being reinforced. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37880795938457) ### ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39591676972825) Provide the options for seam tape extension. _****_ 1. Click on the segment with seam tape applied with ![Seam Taping On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37880812122905) **Seam Taping** tool. 2. Set the**Extend** option in the Property Editor. **N****on****e** | Seam tape does not extend. ---|--- **To Outline** | Extend to the pattern outline. **To Seam Taping** | Extend to another seam tape area of ​​the intersected line. * The arrow highlighted on the segment indicates the direction from start to end. ****📝****Note:**** * When extending a seam tape to another seam taping, please make sure there is an intersected seam tape for reference. * If you apply Seam Taping Extend in the lower version (before ver 2024.2), both Start and End are assigned as To Outline in the higher version.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on reinforcing pattern edges with seam tape to prevent drooping during simulation in CLO 3D.

title: Low-Res Garment
content: **List of Conetents** Low-Res Garment Low-Res Garment Settings **Low-Res Garment ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JQHYRWeRYls \- Decrease general quality of the 3D Garment. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022475628/mceclip0.png) **Low-Res Garment** tool from the 3D toolbar or navigate and select Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Low-Res Garment.** ** Low-Res Garment Settings ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ONAksiYyWLE \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022475648/mceclip1.png) **Low-Res Garment** tool from the 3D toolbar and the Low-Res Properties window will appear. * **Particle Distance** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7hjdc8LLbSs \- Change all Patterns’ Particle Distance to 20mm. \- Modify **Tolerance** to decide the range of Particle Distance so that only Patterns with corresponding Particle Distance value will be affected. Patterns with Add’l Thickness - Collision value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. ** ** * **Skin Offset ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IvPi7Rh80YU \- Change all Avatar’s Skin Offset to the default value, 3mm. \- Modify **Tolerance** to decide the range of Skin Offset so that only Patterns with corresponding Skin Offset value will be affected. title: Copy/Paste/Replace
content: ### **List of Contents** #### **Copy and Paste** #### **Replace** #### Depending on the user's needs, copy and paste patterns or replace them only in the form of a specific pattern while maintaining the original properties. ### #### **Copy and Paste** 1. Click the ![Transform Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879877879705)**Transform Pattern** or ![Edit Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879877892633)E**dit Pattern tool** on the 2D toolbar. 2. Right-click on the pattern or Internal line to be copied. 3. Click the **Copy** (Ctrl+C) menu. 4. **Right-click on the 2D background and click the Paste **(Ctrl+V) menu. 5. Press the Shift key to place it on a vertical/horizontal/45˚ line or freely click anywhere you want. **📝****Note:** * Right-clicking during paste allows you to enter values for Interval/Number of Shapes/Position (Internal Line). * Patterns can be copied and pasted even between multi-run CLO programs. #### #### **Replace** 1. Right-click on the original pattern to be replaced. 2. Click the **Replace** menu. → The pattern is replaced with the copied pattern's segment point locations, curves, notches, baselines, pattern names, and grading information. → Sewing lines, Internal shapes, Graphics, Fabrics, Topstitching, Puckering, and buttons are maintained as the properties of the original pattern. **📝****Note:** Pattern replacement is only possible if the number of Segment points is the same. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879877900697) ### _**![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37879893509529)**_ _****_ Even if the old and new patterns have different segment points, you can easily replace them. 1. Right-click on the original pattern, internal line, internal shape, baseline, or baseline shape to be replaced. 2. Click **Replaced by** menu. → The original pattern or line is replaced with the new one's segment point locations, curves, notches, baselines, pattern names, and grading information. → Sewing lines, Internal shapes, Graphics, Fabrics, Topstitching, Puckering, and buttons are maintained as the properties of the original pattern. 3. Select the new pattern, internal line, internal shape, baseline, or baseline shape. → W**hen the number of segment points is the**same** , t**he replacement process will be completed automatically. 4. Click and match the Segment point from the original pattern to the new pattern. **→** W**hen the number of segment points**differs** , the Segment point matching action is required. → ****After matching enough Segment points,****t** he replacement process will be completed automatically. 5. **Press the**Enter** key to complete if enough core points have been matched or if there are no more points to match.** **📝 Note:** * If both the original and new patterns are half-symmetry, their center points will automatically align. * **For unclosed****internal shapes or baseline shapes, their endpoints are automatically matched. ** * **Press the Delete to cancel the last step, or****Press the Esc key to cancel all actions** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to effectively copy, paste, and replace patterns in your design software while preserving their original properties.

title: Freeze/Unfreeze
content: **Objective** Use this function to fasten patterns like solid objects. Deactivated patterns do not collide during simulation, however, frozen patterns do (they maintain collision). Therefore, it is better to use for draping multiple layered garments. For instance, draping and freezing inner garments first, then draping outerwear above helps avoid occasional instabilities. **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490267/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490287/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated above. 2. Right-click on the 3D or 2D pattern and click **Freeze/Unfreeze.** → The pattern selected is frozen/unfrozen. **※Note:** Right-click in the empty space of the 3D window and hover over **Show/Hide Color** , then click******Show Freeze** to show or hide the color applied during freeze. (ver 6.1)
content_description: This webpage provides a guide on using the freeze/unfreeze function in Clo3D to effectively manage layered garment draping and maintain collision during simulations.
